What you’ll do in this role:
• Conduct functional assessments which include initial reviews, face-to-face, video or telephone assessments to evaluate how a claimant’s health condition or disability affects them for various types of benefit.
• Analyse and interpret clinical information and supporting evidence.
• Write detailed evidence-based reports to support the DWP/DfC in making informed and objective decisions - no treatment or diagnosis required.
• Use IT systems to support clinical decision-making and report writing.
• Develop your clinical knowledge and constantly learn about health conditions which are less familiar to you.
• Develop your clinical knowledge and constantly learn about health conditions which are less familiar to you.
What are PIP and WCA?
• Personal Independence Payment (PIP) is a benefit for people with a long-term health condition or impairment. It is paid to make a contribution to the extra costs that disabled people may face, to help them lead full, active and independent lives.
• Work Capability Assessment (WCA) is a functional assessment that looks at a range of different activities relating to physical, mental, intellectual and cognitive functions, to help DWP determine a customer's capability for work or work-related activity.

Qualifications
About you
•
At least one year of broad post-registration clinical experience working with adult patients
•
Excellent observational, questioning and communication skills, giving you the ability to listen, empathise and dig deeper
•
Ability to produce clear, accurate and detailed reports from multiple information sources
•
Comfortable and able to work quickly to meet structured targets
•
Good IT skills including experience using clinical IT systems, Microsoft Office, and the ability to learn and utilise new systems effectively.

We were awarded two contracts to deliver the Health Assessment Advisory Service (HAAS) assessments in the Midlands and Wales for the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), and in Northern Ireland for the Department for Communities (DfC).
We deliver assessments for a variety of different benefits, including delivering PIP, WCA and Specialist benefit assessments across the Midlands and Wales, and in Northern Ireland.
Security and compliance
Successful candidates will be required to successfully complete government baseline personnel security standard vetting. This is the recognised standard for the pre-employment screening of individuals with access to government asset.

About This Job
Role Overview
Quadient's eInvoicing portfolio is part of our suite of Finance and Communication Automation software solutions, designed to help organizations move from fragmented execution to governed, data-driven control. It connects essential workflows through a unified backbone, with a consistent user experience and shared visibility — so leaders stop chasing numbers across tools and teams.
eInvoicing is one of the fastest growing areas of our portfolio, driven by the acceleration of global mandates including France, Belgium, Germany, UK and the broader EU ViDA framework.
The Head of eInvoicing Product Management lives at the intersection of product strategy, customer insights and engineering execution. The role will define and drive the strategic direction of Quadient’s eInvoicing product portfolio, including our PA/Peppol solution and our Invoice delivery solution. Reporting to the SVP of Product and R&D, this leader owns the product vision, multi‑year roadmap, and business outcomes for one of the most regulated and fastest‑moving categories in B2B SaaS,while leading a global team of product and product marketing leaders.
The role partners closely with R&D, Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Partners, to scale our eInvoicing business across France and the broader EU mandate markets.
Strategic Responsibilities
• Define and communicate a compelling long‑term product vision for Quadient’s eInvoicing portfolio, taking into account how the portfolio supports and provide compliance to the wider suite of Finance and Communication Automation solutions.
• Build and maintain a rolling multi‑year product strategy and roadmap aligned to country mandate timelines (France, Belgium, Germany, UK, EU ViDA, and global rollouts).
• Translate evolving regulatory frameworks — Peppol, PA, CTC models, structured invoicing formats (Factur‑X, UBL, XRechnung) — into differentiated, scalable product capabilities.
• Own the strategy for Quadient’s Peppol Access Point and how the solution integrates within the Quadient portfolio and/or 3rd party partners.
• Lead competitive analysis across the eInvoicing landscape and position Quadient for leadership in mandate markets.
• Represent Quadient externally with strategic customers, partners, regulatory bodies, and industry forums (OpenPeppol, EESPA, national tax authority working groups).
• Support M&A evaluation and post‑acquisition integration for eInvoicing assets and partner networks.
• Own product P&L, with accountability for the financial outcomes of the portfolio.
Product & Portfolio Leadership
• Lead and develop the eInvoicing Product Management and Product Marketing teams, including PMs for SIG, Impress Invoice, and PA/Peppol — setting clear ownership, performance expectations, and growth paths.
• Partner with R&D leadership (eInvoicing pod) to deliver predictable, high‑quality roadmap outcomes against fixed regulatory deadlines.
• Drive modernization toward a cloud‑native, API‑first eInvoicing platform with strong AI‑enabled capabilities for data extraction, validation, and exception handling.
• Establish best‑in‑class product discovery, prioritization, and release governance practices for a portfolio where compliance is non‑negotiable.
• Integrate customer feedback, usage data, compliance signals, and competitive intelligence into every prioritization decision.
• Deliver positioning, sales enablement, and analyst engagement.
Business & Market Impact
• Drive ARR growth, NRR, and cloud adoption across the eInvoicing portfolio, with clear ownership of financial outcomes.
• Partner with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Partner teams to support pipeline, win rates, and time‑to‑value in mandate markets.
• Strengthen Quadient’s presence in analyst evaluations covering eInvoicing,
• Act as a senior product voice in strategic deals sales cycles, executive briefings, and major RFP responses.

Qualifications
• 12-15+ years of product management experience in enterprise SaaS, with at least 3 years in a people management role.
• Direct experience leading eInvoicing, e‑Reporting, , tax compliance, or related Financial Automation products.
• Deep working knowledge of Peppol, EU ViDA, country‑specific CTC models, and structured invoice formats such as UBL, Factur‑X, or XRechnung
• Demonstrated success delivering complex, compliance‑driven platform products on fixed regulatory timelines.
• Strong technical fluency with APIs, integrations, validation/transformation engines, and AI‑enabled workflows.
• Excellent written and verbal communication in English; working French and/or another European language is a strong advantage.
• Experience working across France and the broader EU, with comfort operating in a global, matrixed organization.
Success in the Role
Success will be measured by the clarity and adoption of the eInvoicing product vision, on‑time delivery against country mandate deadlines, ARR and NRR growth within the eInvoicing portfolio, expanded Peppol and partner network reach, and the development of a strong, respected Product team.

Additional Information
Rewards & Benefits
• Flexible Work: Embrace a hybrid work model blending office and remote setup for a balanced lifestyle.
• Endless Learning: Access global opportunities for growth through our 24/7 online learning platform.
• Inclusive Community: Join our Empowered Communities and engage in our Philanthropy program.
• Comprehensive Rewards: Enjoy competitive Total Rewards covering wellness, work/life balance, and more, including a generous referral scheme.
• Caring for Wellbeing: Access our complimentary employee assistance program for mental health support.
Smart Work at Quadient
At Quadient, our Smart Work approach fosters connection, collaboration, and innovation while offering flexibility based on role requirements. Whether on-site, hybrid, or remote, our work environments are designed to support productivity and engagement. Hybrid employees balance remote and in-office work, on-site roles contribute daily to our vibrant workplace culture, and remote employees stay connected through virtual collaboration and in-person events. No matter where you work, you’ll be part of a dynamic, people-first community that drives success together.
Be yourself at Quadient
Our values define how we work as a team: Empowerment, Passion, Inspiration and Community.  They inspire us to be EPIC. Together. What makes Quadient different is how different we are. We’re a team of individuals with one goal but many perspectives. When you connect with Quadient, you become part of a community that cares - in a culture that embraces differences and values every voice.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/williamsracing/.description_excerpt:
About This Job
The Opportunity A lot of designers worry that moving in house means trading interesting work for a single brand book and a slow calendar. That isn’t the role on offer here. Williams F1 Team is rebuilding what its brand means in public, and digital is where most fans meet it  the website, the app, the campaigns that wrap around the season’s biggest moments. You’ll be hands on, shipping work every week alongside an evolving brand system that you’ll help refine as you go. The brand isn’t finished. You won’t be inheriting a museum. This isn’t a social content seat we have a dedicated social team who own the day to day there. Your remit is the bigger, more considered work: the website, the app, integrating with marketing campaigns, performance driven creative, and the digital moments around special races and fan activations. If you’re a strong mid weight pushing into Senior, or a Senior who wants to put their craft against something they actually care about, this is the kind of in house role that doesn’t feel in house.
What You’ll Do:
Website, App & Product Moments
• Design and refine pages, components, editorial moments and email templates for williamsf1.com and the Williams F1 Team app — these are your primary canvases.
• Concept and design launch assets for new app features, product drops and marketing campaigns the wider team is bringing forward.
• Design user experiences across web, app, and fan platforms — memberships, content hubs and interactive features — producing wireframes, prototypes and high-fidelity UI designs.
• Translate fan behaviours, data and testing insights into intuitive, high performing journeys that drive conversion and engagement.
• Partner with product, engineering and data teams to deliver and iterate on digital experiences.
• Build a body of work overtime that visibly improves how the brand expresses itself on its owned digital surfaces.
Fan Growth & Performance Creative
• Design high performing creative for paid and organic channels — social, digital, ecommerce and app.
• Develop and iterate creative assets for multichannel performance marketing campaigns (Meta, TikTok, Google, williamsf1.com, Williams F1 App, and more).
• Own creative testing cycles — A/B and multivariate testing — to continuously improve engagement and conversion.
• Rapidly iterate assets based on performance signals (CTR, engagement, retention, conversion).
• Develop scalable creative systems and templates for continuous experimentation.
• Build assets that support the full fan journey — from acquisition through to engagement and retention.
• Collaborate with growth, media and analytics teams to translate performance data into creative improvement.
Key Campaign Moments
• Lead the creative for the season’s biggest activations — special races like the British Grand Prix at Silverstone and the Las Vegas GP, custom livery reveals, fanzone activations and the digital campaigns that wrap around them.
• Partner closely with the Fan Growth & Performance team to deliver high quality assets on fast turnarounds — the calendar is unforgiving and a good idea on Tuesday often needs to ship on Thursday.
• Create content for both race and non race weekend storytelling and always on digital to social loops, optimised for reach and interaction.
• Contribute to specific social led campaigns alongside our dedicated social team, bringing the bigger campaign moments when a unified creative is needed.
Brand & Design System
• Work alongside the Senior Design Manager and the rest of the creative team to evolve Williams’ visual identity — informed by what’s actually performing in market and feedback from the teams using the brand day to day.
• Help maintain and improve brand guidelines, motion principles and component library as we ship more work.
• Champion a fan first and data informed mindset across all outputs.
• Spot opportunities where the brand could be sharper, weirder, more confident — and bring them forward
How You’ll Work
• Take a brief end to end — understand the ask, propose a direction, present it, take feedback and ship.
• Bridge brand storytelling with performance marketing and product UX, ensuring consistency across marketing creative, paid media and product design.
• Partner with marketing, fan engagement, content producers, photographers, motion designers and external partners.
• Manage your own workload across multiple parallel briefs at race week tempo.

Qualifications
• 5–7 years of design experience, with a strong portfolio demonstrating both performance driven creative (paid social, campaigns) and digital product / UX work (web, app). Sports, entertainment, lifestyle or premium consumer brand backgrounds are especially welcome — but a brilliant portfolio from anywhere matters more than the industry on your CV.
• Your portfolio shows real campaigns and live products, not just unbriefed concepts.
• Strong typographic and layout craft across digital, campaign and motion led formats.
• Expert in Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, After Effects) and Figma.
• Proven experience designing for paid media and growth focused environments, with strong understanding of creative testing, optimisation and data informed design.
• Comfortable working across web, app and campaign formats — you understand that a hero banner, an app onboarding screen and a Silverstone fanzone graphic each demand different thinking, even when they’re telling the same brand story.
• Collaborative, calm under pressure, opinionated about craft but not precious about feedback. You can work fast when the calendar demands it without dropping the quality bar.
• Genuinely care about Formula 1 — or are clearly the kind of person who falls hard for the sports they get close to.
• Bachelor’s degree in Graphic Design, Digital Media or a related field preferred; portfolio over credentials.

Additional Information
Atlassian Williams F1 Team is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity and inclusion. We are happy to discuss reasonable job adjustments.

They will be responsible for providing Legionella control services, maintaining compliance with ACOP L8, and building strong, lasting relationships with both internal and external customers.

• Deliver on-site service, chemical treatment analysis, monitoring and operational support to existing customers

• Demonstrate passion for customer satisfaction and relationship development

• Proven technical competence and excellent customer problem solving skills

• Good literacy and numeracy skills

• Availability to travel within the assigned area, including overnight stops
Desirable:
• Google Suite
• Experience of working in a large corporate environment
• Experience in Water Industry
• Legionella training certification

To make buying at Wise as seamless and frictionless as sending money across borders.

This is your chance to help shape what Procurement looks like at Wise — providing an exceptional standard of customer service, building scalable processes, driving innovation, and helping us create a best-in-class global procurement function from the ground up!

Manage a team of 2x Procurement professionals helping them to navigate complexity through effective coaching and development strategies.

Mentor and develop procurement team members, fostering a culture of continuous improvement and professional growth.

Choose your path to impact. As a Lead You’ll take ownership from day one. Of course, you will have feedback from smart, curious people across Wise but you’ll experience unique levels of ownership and empowerment within your role.

Be extremely hands on. No far away leaders in Wise, and in this role you’d be expected to take on the work yourself.

Be part of our mission to make money without borders the new normal.

Project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously.

A get-it-done, collaborative approach to problem-solving.

About This Job
Are you motivated by solving complex supply chain and procurement challenges in highly regulated, mission-critical industries?
Our Defence and Security team is looking for an experienced supply chain professional to help clients improve the performance, resilience and readiness of their supply chains. You may already work in Defence, or you may bring relevant experience from aerospace, nuclear, energy, oil and gas, advanced manufacturing or another complex industrial sector.
You will join our growing Defence Supply Chain team, working with public and private-sector clients in the UK and internationally. You will help clients address challenges such as strengthening supplier performance, accelerating production, improving supply chain resilience, transforming procurement and making better decisions across complex international supply networks.
This is an opportunity to apply practical industry experience to some of the most important supply chain challenges facing Defence and national security. You will combine your knowledge of supply chain, procurement or manufacturing environments with PA’s strategy, technology and transformation capabilities to help clients deliver lasting results.
We are particularly interested in candidates who have developed their careers within industrial supply chains, procurement organisations or manufacturing environments and would like to apply that experience to Defence and national security challenges.
You will have opportunity to:
•
Work with Defence organisations, manufacturers and their suppliers to improve supply chain performance, resilience and readiness.
•
Help clients understand and manage complex international supply chains and multi-tier supplier networks.
•
Develop and implement supply chain, procurement and supplier-management strategies.
•
Support clients to strengthen supplier performance, manage supply chain risk and address constraints affecting production and delivery.
•
Help organisations improve planning, forecasting, sourcing, inventory, supplier collaboration and operational decision-making.
•
Support production ramp-up, manufacturing scale-up and operational readiness programmes.
•
Design and deliver supply chain and procurement transformation programmes, from initial analysis through to implementation.
•
Use data, analytics and digital technology to improve supply chain visibility and support better decisions.
•
Work with senior client stakeholders across commercial, procurement, supply chain, operations, engineering and programme teams.
•
Contribute to the continued growth of PA’s Defence Supply Chain business, including developing propositions, supporting business development and sharing your expertise with colleagues.

Qualifications
Essential experience:
You will bring:
•
Experience working within complex industrial supply chains in Defence, aerospace, nuclear, energy, oil and gas, manufacturing or similarly regulated sectors.
•
Experience in supply chain, procurement, supplier management, planning, operations or a related discipline.
•
Experience working with complex supplier ecosystems, international supply chains or global sourcing arrangements.
•
A track record of delivering supply chain, procurement or operational improvement programmes.
•
Strong analytical, problem-solving and stakeholder management skills.
•
The ability to work collaboratively with clients and adapt your experience to new environments and challenges.
Desirable experience:
Experience in one or more of the following would be beneficial:
•
Supply chain transformation, resilience or risk management.
•
Strategic sourcing, supplier development or supplier performance improvement.
•
Supply chain design, modelling or network optimisation.
•
Production ramp-up, manufacturing scale-up or operational readiness programmes.
•
Application of digital, data and analytics solutions within supply chain environments.
•
Consulting or client-facing transformation experience.
•
MCIPS, CIPS, APICS/ASCM, CILT or equivalent professional qualifications.
The type of person who will succeed in this role:
You will enjoy solving difficult problems and working with clients to turn analysis into practical change. You will be comfortable moving between strategic questions and the operational realities of suppliers, factories, programmes and international supply networks.
You do not need to have spent your whole career in Defence. We value the experience and different perspectives that candidates from adjacent industrial sectors can bring. What matters is your ability to understand complex supply chain and procurement challenges and apply your experience in a Defence environment.
We know the skill-gap and ‘somewhat need to tick every box’ can get in the way of meeting brilliant candidates, so please don’t hesitate to apply – we’d love to hear from you.
Apply today by completing our online application
Please be aware that some of our UK roles at PA Consulting require a UK security clearance.
All PA people are required to undergo background checks and to achieve the Baseline Personnel Security Standard however, some UK roles also require higher levels of National Security Vetting, where applicants must have at least 5 years of continuous residency in the UK.
We therefore ask that you only apply if you meet the residency requirements (i.e. you are a British citizen or have been resident in the UK for the past 5 years), as this is the prerequisite for a security clearance. If you're unsure about your eligibility, we encourage you to review the UK Government’s guidance on security vetting before applying.

Additional Information
Working arrangements
We work in a hybrid way, combining time in the office, on client sites and working remotely. Our general approach is to spend a minimum of two days each week in an office or on a client site, although this will vary by role and assignment.
Some assignments may require regular travel and periods of up to five days each week at a client site.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/ifs1/7440001550.description_excerpt:
About This Job
Build and operate the interface, semantic layer and controls that let AI agents work inside IFS software safely.
This role is hybrid or remote.
The role:
You will own the web client of an AI agent product for our enterprise customers. It is a React and TypeScript single-page application, and almost everything on its screen arrives as a stream from a language-model agent.
What you will do:
• Build an interface that people can trust while the content on it is still arriving, changing and occasionally wrong.
• Turn what the agent produces into a usable interface: prose, generated views and actions the user can take.
• Make sure the agent acts only with the user's explicit consent, and that people can always see what it did and why.
• Own the front-end architecture, the component system and the contracts with the teams behind the agent.
• Help move the interface towards Lit and Web Components, so that what we build is standards-based and not tied to a single framework or application.
• Treat accessibility, performance, testing and observability as part of the product rather than a late pass.
• Work across the boundary into the services your interface depends on, then ship what you build and run it in production.
Why it is interesting:
Most front-end work assumes that a page loads and is then correct. Here the content arrives in pieces, gets revised, sometimes fails partway and is sometimes wrong. And some of it is code a model wrote, which the browser should not trust. The protocols involved are young and still changing (AG-UI, A2UI, MCP Apps). You will help shape them, not just consume them.
What we are looking for:
• Substantial production single-page applications, built and operated, with real depth in TypeScript and React.
• Asynchronous state you can reason about.
• Browser security as a working concern: iframe sandboxing, postMessage, Content Security Policy, sanitising content you did not write.
• Component and design-system work in a shared codebase, including web components used inside React.
• Accessibility as a practice. You know how to keep it tested.
• Willing to write Go and to read Python. Prior experience in either is not required.
• Test-first habits and continuous delivery.
• Clear writing. Decisions are recorded as short architecture decision records (ADRs), and protocols are documented before they change.
• Comfortable working with AI coding agents as part of how you build.
Also valuable:
• A product surface built on a language model in production: streaming, partial output, retries, and showing uncertainty.
• Hands-on knowledge of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and MCP Apps, AG-UI or A2UI.
• Experience building with Lit and Web Components, including shadow DOM and custom elements used from other frameworks.
• Expression languages or compilers.
• A platform where behaviour is configured through data or metadata rather than written in code.
• Data visualisation.
• Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes and Helm.
• Knowledge of an enterprise domain: asset management, field service, manufacturing, supply chain.

Qualifications
•
Production experience building and operating substantial single-page applications, with real depth in modern TypeScript and a current framework such as Angular or React.
•
Built a product surface on top of a language model in production: streaming, partial output, cancellation, retries, and what to show when the system is uncertain.
•
Component architecture and design-system work in a codebase other teams contribute to.
•
Accessibility as a working practice, and performance work you can describe in numbers.
•
Comfortable across the boundary: you can write the service-side code your surface needs.
•
Automated testing, observability and continuous delivery as part of how you build.
Also valuable
•
A platform where behaviour is configured through data or metadata rather than written in code.
•
Mobile or progressive web applications, including offline behaviour and poor connectivity.
•
Voice interfaces.
•
Enterprise software domains: asset management, field service, manufacturing, supply chain.

Additional Information
We believe that coming together as a community, in person, is important for innovation, connection and fostering a sense of belonging. Our roles have the right balance of remote and in-office working to enable flexibility for managing your life along with ensuring a real connection with your colleagues and the broader IFS community.

About This Job
We are looking for a hands-on PostgreSQL DBA to help manage database services across our on-premises infrastructure and GCP. The role combines production operations with project work, including migration from Community PostgreSQL to EDB Postgres, high-availability standardization, database consolidation, and operational automation.
You will work closely with DBAs, SRE, infrastructure, application, and security teams. We need someone who can assess the current environment, identify risks and improvements, recommend practical solutions, and follow them through to stable production operations.
Here are the core functions, responsibilities, and expectations for this role:
• PostgreSQL and EDB administration. Administer the full database lifecycle, including installation, configuration, patching, upgrades, capacity planning, security, monitoring, incident response, and decommissioning.
• High availability with EFM. Configure, operate, monitor, and troubleshoot EDB Failover Manager clusters; perform planned switchovers and failover tests; validate application connectivity; and safely reintegrate failed or former primary nodes.
• Backup and recovery with Barman. Configure and monitor base backups and WAL archiving or streaming, manage retention, execute point-in-time recovery, and conduct documented restore and disaster-recovery tests against agreed RPO and RTO targets.
• Monitoring and alerting with PEM. Register and manage servers and agents, configure meaningful metrics and alert thresholds, investigate alerts and performance trends using graphs, and maintain notification and escalation integrations.
• Automation and version control. Use TPA and Ansible/Spacelift to build repeatable PostgreSQL/EDB environments and maintain playbooks and configuration in Git and GitHub using branches, pull requests, and peer review.
• Replication and recovery. Configure and troubleshoot physical streaming and logical replication, replication slots, WAL retention, lag, and timeline issues; use pg_rewind when appropriate to resynchronize a node after timelines diverge.
• Performance engineering. Analyze execution plans and wait or lock behavior, tune SQL and indexes, and optimize PostgreSQL and operating-system settings, including autovacuum, memory, storage, and checkpoint or WAL behavior.
• Connectivity and security. Operate PgBouncer and manage roles, privileges, authentication, pg_hba.conf, TLS, secrets, and least-privilege access in line with organizational standards.
• Migrations and consolidation. Plan and execute major and minor version upgrades, Community PostgreSQL-to-EDB migrations, and database consolidation with validated rollback, testing, and minimal downtime.
• Operational ownership. Create runbooks and architecture documentation, participate in change and incident processes, collaborate with engineering teams, and join an on-call rotation for production emergencies.
• Additional tasks associated with this position may be assigned in response to company initiatives and business needs.
More information about this role:
This is a full-time and remote position based in the U.K. The target compensation package for this role is between GBP 50,000 and 54,000, subject upon internal equity and years of experience.  We may make further adjustments through an approval process if the targeted compensation range needs to be modified based on business needs and market trends.

Qualifications

About This Job
We are looking for a client-facing Security Operations Consultant to join our Digital Trust & Cyber Security practice. Working on behalf of our clients, you will lead Security Operations Centre (SOC) analysts and incident response specialists.
• This is not an INTERNAL SOC ROLE.
• The Ideal candidate will bring a mixture of technical and strong client/stakeholder management.
• The role could include supporting clients in enhancing their SecOps environments to providing hands on active support.
• The candidate should feel comfortable in fast paced environments and client environments.
You will combine hands-on operational leadership with advisory work. This means managing live incident containment and day-to-day SOC operations, while helping enterprise and public sector clients modernise their security operations, improve their SIEM, SOAR and EDR capabilities, and build stronger cyber resilience.
Why consider joining our Digital & Data community? 🤔
• Join our Digital & Data team and work alongside cyber security, product, design and technology specialists in cross-disciplinary teams to solve complex client challenges and bring ideas to life.
• Build a flexible and distinctive career in a trust-based, inclusive environment that values excellence, innovation and curiosity. You can progress through a technical career track without needing to follow the Partner career track if that does not align with your ambitions.
• Work across a broad range of Security Operations engagements, client environments and technology stacks spanning seven sectors. No two projects are the same.
• Join a supportive and collaborative cyber and technology community, with knowledge sharing, peer support, coaching and mentoring from other specialists.
• Deepen your expertise through our culture of learning and growth, with access to a development budget for technical and non-technical training and professional certifications.
• Benefit from a hybrid working approach, with an expectation of being in the office or on a client site for a minimum of two days per week, depending on the role and assignment.
What you'll do 🌱
• Lead and develop SOC analysts and incident response specialists, providing clear operational direction, coaching and support across day-to-day security operations.
• Take a hands-on leadership role during cyber security incidents, coordinating investigation, containment, eradication, recovery, stakeholder communications and post-incident reviews.
• Help enterprise and public sector clients assess and improve their Security Operations capabilities, identifying gaps across people, processes and technology and translating these into practical improvements.
• Advise on the evolution and optimisation of SIEM, SOAR, EDR and threat-detection tooling to improve visibility, reduce noise and strengthen detection and response capabilities.
• Develop and maintain incident playbooks, standard operating procedures, automated response workflows and proactive tabletop exercises.
• Support the development of modern Security Operations services and ways of working, sharing your expertise across our Digital Trust & Cyber Security community through coaching, mentoring and knowledge sharing.
Security technologies you'll work with 🚀
We advocate using the right technology for the right task. Depending on the client environment and engagement, you can expect to work across technologies including:
• SIEM and security analytics platforms, such as Microsoft Sentinel and Splunk.
• SOAR and security automation technologies used for enrichment, triage and response orchestration.
• Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR/XDR) platforms, such as Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and CrowdStrike Falcon.
• Threat intelligence, detection engineering, investigation and incident response technologies.
• Cloud security monitoring across Microsoft Azure, AWS and GCP environments.
What you can expect 🌱
• Work collaboratively across multiple technical teams and stakeholder groups, using your Security Operations expertise to solve complex client problems and contribute to internal initiatives.
• Participate in live, in-person working sessions to investigate incidents, assess operational challenges and design practical improvements, alongside asynchronous collaboration through Microsoft Teams.
• Work with the team at client sites or in our offices for a minimum of two days per week. The time you spend and where you work will vary by role and assignment, including the possibility of being on a client site for up to five days per week.
• Work in an environment that takes its values seriously and places collaboration, inclusion, learning and client impact at the heart of how teams operate.

Qualifications
Essential requirements ✅
Even if you don’t meet every requirement below, feel free to still apply as we are often hiring for similar roles which your background might be better suited to.
• SOC Leadership: Experience running or supervising a SOC, CSOC, or Incident Response team.
• Incident Response: Practical experience managing live cyber incidents (such as ransomware, account takeovers, or supply chain breaches).
• Technical Stack: Direct experience working with major SIEM/SOAR tools (e.g., Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk) and EDR/XDR platforms (e.g., Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, CrowdStrike Falcon).
• Security Frameworks: Solid understanding of MITRE ATT&CK, NIST CSF, NCSC Caf v4.0 and ISO 27001.
• Communication: Ability to write concise incident reports and speak comfortably with both engineers and business leaders.
Desirable
• Experience working in management consulting, managed services (MSSP), or client-facing advisory roles.
• Experience in regulated UK environments (such as Central Government,  Defence, or Critical National Infrastructure).
• Hands-on familiarity with cloud security monitoring in AWS, Azure, or GCP.
Please be aware that some of our UK roles at PA Consulting require a UK security clearance.
All PA people are required to undergo background checks and to achieve the Baseline Personnel Security Standard however, some UK roles also require higher levels of National Security Vetting, where applicants must have at least 5 years of continuous residency in the UK.
We therefore ask that you only apply if you meet the residency requirements (i.e. you are a British citizen or have been resident in the UK for the past 5 years), as this is the prerequisite for a security clearance. If you're unsure about your eligibility, we encourage you to review the UK Government’s guidance on security vetting before applying.

Additional Information
Assessment process ⚖️
Please note that the interview stages may be subject to change based on the specific requirements of the role.
• Quick call with one of our Tech Recruiters – to discuss your application, the role and PA
• Round 1: Either a competency or technical interview (60 mins)
• Round 2: Either a competency or technical interview, whichever you didn’t do at first

About This Job
About the role
Giving back to the communities we work in, and those our customers serve, is a core part of how Version 1 delivers value. Our work has won a Princess Royal Training Award, and our social value framework holds a Silver Social Value Quality Mark accreditation.
This is a senior role in our commercial function, owning social value propositions and partnerships across Version 1. Working alongside our ESG team and delivery practices, you will build the partner network and the propositions our social value commitments come from, including joint propositions with community, education, SME and hyperscaler partners.
You will shape strategy aligned to our sector and account plans, engaging customers early and designing social value programmes we can deliver at scale. You will write the social value content on our largest pursuits, and set and assure the standard on the rest, scored against the criteria each customer has published.
Regular travel to customers, partners and sector events is expected, with more during live deals. You will engage at SRO and commercial director level with customers, and with partner leadership, Version 1 account directors and our executive team.
What you'll do
Own Version 1’s social value development
•
Own and run a rolling gap analysis of where we stand against the criteria we are scored on, covering data, process, partner coverage and delivery evidence.
•
Decide how gaps get closed, and make the investment case for new partnerships, changes to practice or new capability.

Review scoring feedback and debriefs after every bid, and act on what the evaluator told us.

Build social value capability across commercial and delivery teams through guidance, templates and training.

Set the approach to Procurement Act 2023 transparency data.
•
Design repeatable social value solutions that bid teams can tailor rather than rebuild each time.

Line manage and develop the social value team.

About This Job
We are seeking a Data Scientist to design and deliver analytical models and decision-support systems that improve understanding, prediction and decision-making across the business.
The role focuses on building practical models of complex real-world systems, working with imperfect data, uncertainty and competing objectives to generate commercially valuable outcomes.
Responsible for developing deployable analytical solutions in partnership with Engineering teams, while not owning production infrastructure or application development.
Key Responsibilities:
Model Development
• Design, develop and maintain statistical, probabilistic and simulation-based models.
• Translate complex business questions into tractable modelling problems.
• Select appropriate modelling approaches based on the characteristics of the problem rather than methodological preference.
• Develop prototypes and working solutions iteratively, refining approaches as new information becomes available.
• Build analytical assets that can be reused as products, decision-support tools or operational capabilities.
• Design and analyse experiments to evaluate interventions, operational changes and model effectiveness.
Inference & Uncertainty
• Work effectively with incomplete, imperfect and evolving datasets.
• Develop approaches for estimating missing information and combining evidence from multiple sources.
• Quantify uncertainty and communicate appropriate confidence in model outputs.
• Test assumptions and identify limitations within modelling approaches.

Please note, this role operates on a hybrid working model and requires a minimum of three days per week at our WCA Assessment Centre in Romford.
The Clinical Standards Lead will work closely with both new and experienced Functional Assessors to provide supervision and feedback, utilising quality and productivity data to enable professional development in line with the Performance Excellence Framework.
The successful applicant will also need to maintain their DWP approval by carrying out assessments to evaluate the overall functional effects of the Claimant’s health condition and or disability on their everyday life, following the WCA guidelines. Assessors will be expected to use DWP processes and systems and conduct high quality assessments in an empathetic and professional manner.
Responsibilities:
• Carry out regular 1:1 supervision, clinical observations, and dip tests/ live dip tests (audits), coaching HPs in line with defined Support Pathways based on quality performance related risk assessments.
• Monitor trends and specific emerging issues that need to be addressed, delivering group quality improvement sessions where common issues are apparent.
• Supervise the support pathways of Functional Assessors as defined within the Performance Excellence Framework, utilising clinical audit and quality outcomes with a view to achieving sustained quality improvement within the contract.
• Carry out telephone, video and/ or face-to-face functional assessments to establish any functional restriction caused by a claimant’s health concern. Be the point of contact during the consultation stage for claimants with a wide range of health conditions and disabilities.
• Obtain evidence from the claimant, using active listening and asking appropriate questions to establish any functional restriction.
• Apply critical thinking and logical reasoning to produce accurate, and detailed reports, utilising DWP systems and processes.
• Ensure that reports are completed to a high standard to achieve the required quality grades, including in relation to accurate spelling and grammar.
• Support achievement of service delivery KPIs through provision of an effective and efficient Assessment Service.
• Liaise with a range of clinical peers across the NHS and private healthcare sector, charities, and support organisations to obtain and evaluate evidence that assists in the production of detailed reports.
• Proactively develop knowledge of health conditions through engaging with Continuous Professional Development (CPD) opportunities in line with professional registration and contractual requirements.
• Undertake any training required to carry out Functional Assessor role e.g., Paper-based Reviews and initial Triage.
• Take ownership of professional revalidation to ensure that this is completed within the required timescales.

Qualifications

• A minimum of 12 months experience as a DWP approved Functional Assessor, achieving consistently high-quality clinical audit outcomes.
• Be HCPC / NMC/ GMC registered with no restrictions on practice.
• Have a proven record of proactively engaging with relevant Continual Professional Development (CPD).
• Broad-ranging clinical experience across a range on conditions, including working with adults.
• Demonstrable knowledge of the clinical aspects and likely functional effects of a wide range of medical conditions, including skills in assessing people and the ability to perform a relevant examination.
• Knowledge and skills in assessing people with conditions affecting mental health, intellectual and cognitive function including the ability to perform a relevant examination.
• Ability to critically evaluate evidence and use logical reasoning to provide accurate evidence-based advice.
• Have excellent interpersonal and written communication skills that include the ability to interact sensitively and appropriately, take a comprehensive, history; accurately recording clinical findings, producing succinct, accurate reports in Plain English, while utilising a questioning style that allows the Claimant to talk freely about their level of function.

• Efficient IT skills and an ability to type notes accurately whilst conducting assessments (30 words per minute minimum).
• Ability to maintain a strong work ethic while working independently.
• Ability and willingness to share clinical experience and knowledge to positive effect within a team.
• Comfortable working to team and individual targets.

The child has a complex clinical profile, including:
• Pontocerebellar Hypoplasia

They are also oxygen dependent (requiring up to 2L via nasal prongs) and need ongoing respiratory support, including:

• Being around others and included in conversation

About This Job
About the role
The HPC Lead is responsible for owning and evolving the High Performance Computing infrastructure for R&D scientists, including clusters, GPU provisioning, storage, and notebook infrastructure. This role serves as the technical and strategic anchor for HPC workloads for scientific computing and adjacent AI/ML needs. You will combine platform strategy, architecture, operational leadership, and partnership with scientific stakeholders while acting as a senior, hands-on contributor.
What you will do
•
Own the HPC infrastructure and work directly with engineers on cluster configuration, GPU provisioning, storage tier management, scheduler tuning, and notebook infrastructure.
•
Define and own the HPC architecture roadmap, including cluster topology, GPU fleet composition, storage architecture, job-scheduling strategy, and the trajectory toward modern orchestration.
•
Drive GPU procurement and investment strategy, evaluating vendor proposals critically, and making investment decisions with architectural confidence.
•
Manage HPC capacity plans, hardware maintenance, support vendors, and contractor relationships, defining SLA design and the build-versus-buy decision for physical maintenance.
•
Partner closely with scientists, computational specialists, and bioinformaticians to understand their workloads and ensure the HPC estate meets their evolving requirements.
•
Use AI coding and productivity tools for automation scripts, infrastructure-as-code, operational runbooks, and performance analysis.
•
Lead, mentor, and develop engineering teams to drive technical excellence, foster a culture of continuous improvement, and build deep HPC expertise across the organization.
•
Establish and monitor HPC performance metrics, KPIs, and optimization targets; conduct regular performance profiling and capacity forecasting to ensure efficient resource utilization.
•
Develop and maintain comprehensive documentation, operational runbooks, and knowledge management systems to ensure operational continuity and enable team self-sufficiency.
•
Oversee budget planning, financial forecasting, and strategic procurement decisions for HPC infrastructure investments, ensuring cost-effectiveness and alignment with organizational priorities.
•
Establish and enforce security protocols, compliance standards, and disaster recovery procedures for the HPC environment, ensuring business continuity and data protection.
•
Communicate HPC strategy, status, and recommendations to executive stakeholders and cross-functional teams, translating technical concepts for non-technical audiences.

Qualifications
**Required Qualifications**
• Expert-level depth in HPC infrastructure, including cluster management, GPU provisioning (NVIDIA, A100/H100 generation), MPI, storage (Lustre, NFS, object storage), and job scheduling.
• Expert understanding of GPU architecture, including generations, interconnects (NVLink, InfiniBand), memory profiles, and their implications for scientific workloads.
• Strong experience with modern orchestration and the architectural trajectory toward Kubernetes-native HPC environments (e.g., GPU operators, Kubernetes scheduler extensions).
• Strong strategic capability in defining maintenance and support strategies, evaluating vendor contract structures, and managing hardware investments.
• Strong ability to understand scientific workloads, conversing credibly with computational scientists and bioinformaticians to translate their needs into infrastructure solutions.
• Strong proficiency in using AI-assisted engineering tools as a primary workflow for infrastructure automation.
• Demonstrated leadership experience managing and mentoring technical teams, with a track record of building high-performing engineering organizations and fostering a culture of continuous improvement.
• Proven expertise in budget planning, financial forecasting, and strategic procurement decisions for technology infrastructure investments.
• Experience establishing and monitoring performance metrics, KPIs, and optimization targets; demonstrated capability in capacity forecasting and resource utilization analysis.
• Strong background in developing and maintaining comprehensive documentation, operational runbooks, and knowledge management systems for complex technical environments.
**Bonus Points**
• Experience in agriculture, life sciences, scientific computing, or a regulated enterprise environment.
• Experience building platforms, products, or services used by multiple internal teams.
• Experience working in distributed, international engineering organisations.
• Familiarity with popular scientific computing frameworks and libraries (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch, HPC libraries).
• Background in security protocols, compliance standards, and disaster recovery procedures for enterprise infrastructure environments.
• Experience communicating complex technical concepts to executive stakeholders and cross-functional teams.

The chance to work as part of a global team to address the current and future needs of the agricultural sector.

Learning culture and wide range of training options.

About This Job
• Job Title - Senior Manager - Restructuring Advisory
• Location – London
• Job Type - Permanent – Full Time – Onsite
Role overview:
FRP Advisory is seeking a highly skilled and experienced Senior Manager in the Restructuring Advisory practice in our London office. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in restructuring advisory services, with extensive experience in a professional services environment. The role will primarily focus on distressed advisory work, such as contingency planning engagements, options analysis, cash flow reviews, and monitoring and critical cash management. The role will also require knowledge and experience of UK insolvency processes and, where required, an ability to take a lead role on insolvency appointments.
This role requires a strategic thinker with a hands-on approach to managing complex restructuring situations and providing exceptional client service. The role will be hands on, the candidate will need to be confident report writer and financial analyst as well as being accomplished at managing and developing less experienced team members.
The candidate should be prepared to input into the growth strategy of the Restructuring Advisory practice, including contributing to publications, marketing collateral, and business development strategy.
Key Responsibilities:

• Lead and manage restructuring advisory projects from inception to completion.
• Where required, perform a senior role on insolvency engagements with a focus on strategy and operations.
• Build and sustain excellent relationships with clients, establishing both a rapport and trust and assume ownership of client relationships.
• Be a first point of client contact.
• Focus on pre-appointment advice, with involvement in formal restructuring processes as required.
• Experience of delivering both mid-market and larger scale assignments, with ability to quickly understand complex group structures and situations, prioritising key issues and delivering insightful analysis and recommendations. In most cases this will involve reporting directly to partners and clients.
• Conduct financial analysis and report writing for partner review.
• Review work of junior team members, providing guidance and close supervision in more complex areas or where team is less experienced.
• Develop and present strategic recommendations to clients.

• Build and maintain strong client relationships, ensuring high levels of client satisfaction.
• Support the senior Restructuring Advisory team in business development to enhance FRP’s profile in restructuring advisory matters
• Lead on preparation and support on delivery of pitches and presentations to potential clients.
• Support Restructuring Advisory directors in targeting and retaining key clients and work providers.
• Actively cultivate a wide network of professionals and corporates from which to generate leads and client work.
• Act as a representative of the firm and department at events.
• Identify new project opportunities and support partners to deliver the Restructuring Advisory team strategy.
• Team Leadership:
• Lead and mentor the junior restructuring advisory team in London.
• Collaborate with other FRP pillars and offices to leverage expertise and resources.
• Ensure compliance with local and international regulations.

Qualifications
• ACA/ACCA qualified or equivalent.
• Minimum of 5 years of experience in restructuring advisory
• CII qualification is preferred, but not a requirement
• Strong leadership and team management skills.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
Personal Attributes:
• Strategic thinker with a proactive approach.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• High level of integrity and professionalism.
• Ability to build and maintain strong relationships.
• Adaptable and resilient in the face of challenges.
• Excellent organisational and time management skills.
• Aligned to FRP’s values

Additional Information
Our Values
• Straightforward: We provide clear, no-nonsense advice.
• Confident: Our guidance is backed by expertise and evidence.
• Pragmatic: We focus on practical solutions and tangible outcomes.
• Real: We are professional yet approachable, understanding the challenges our clients face.
Our Commitment to You and the Environment
At FRP, sustainability is integral to our strategy and operations. Our sustainability depends on building and maintaining meaningful, long-term relationships with all our stakeholders – including our employees, clients, and local communities – while also reducing our impact on the natural environment.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/scalian/7440001.description_excerpt:
About This Job
We are looking for experienced Configuration Managers to join an engineering team in Pitstone.
The team is looking for two Configuration Managers with around 5+ years' experience and one Senior/Lead Configuration Manager with significant Configuration Management experience.
The role will be responsible for effective Configuration Management across complex engineering projects, maintaining configuration baselines, controlling engineering changes, and ensuring accurate and traceable product information throughout the product lifecycle.
The team has recently migrated to a Windchill PLM environment, creating a strong focus on data quality, configuration governance, product structures, and the alignment of engineering information across PLM, ERP, drawings and BOMs.
Key Responsibilities:
• Develop and maintain Configuration Management Plans for new and existing projects.
• Provide Configuration Management guidance to project and engineering teams.
• Define and maintain Configuration Items (CIs), product structures and Bills of Materials (BOMs).
• Establish and maintain configuration baselines, including Functional, Allocated and Product Baselines.
• Manage configuration identification and ensure product information is correctly structured and controlled within the PLM environment.
• Analyse engineering and PLM data to identify configuration gaps, inconsistencies and data-quality issues.
• Ensure consistency between PLM, ERP, engineering drawings, specifications and BOM structures.
• Coordinate configuration change control processes and support Change Control Boards (CCBs).
• Ensure engineering changes are documented, assessed, approved, implemented and fully traceable.
• Maintain accurate configuration status records and documentation throughout the product lifecycle.
• Participate in engineering and design reviews, including PDR and CDR.
• Support configuration audits and ensure compliance with relevant standards and processes.
• Establish, maintain and release configuration documentation at key project milestones.
• Work closely with Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain and Project Management teams.
• Identify opportunities to improve Configuration Management processes, tools and governance.
• Support continuous improvement of configuration data integrity and product information management within the PLM environment.

Qualifications
Requirements:
• Minimum 5 years' experience in Configuration Management within an engineering, technical or data management environment.
• Strong knowledge of Configuration Management principles, processes and best practices.
• Working knowledge of ISO 10007.
• Strong understanding of configuration planning, identification, control, status accounting and configuration audits.
• Strong understanding of technical documentation, product structures, BOMs, Configuration Items and configuration baselines.
• Experience with engineering change management, change control and configuration traceability.
• Experience with PLM/PDM systems, ideally Windchill, Teamcenter, ENOVIA or similar.
• Ability to analyse engineering/product data and identify inconsistencies or configuration issues.
• Good understanding of the relationship between PLM, ERP, drawings, specifications and BOM/product structures.
• Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
• Ability to work autonomously within a multidisciplinary engineering environment.
• CMII certification or equivalent practical Configuration Management experience would be advantageous.
• Relevant higher education qualification or equivalent professional experience.
Desirable:
• Experience within Aerospace, Space, Defence/Military, Automotive or other highly regulated engineering environments.
• Experience with Windchill, particularly configuration management, product structures, BOMs, data quality or PLM migration.
• Experience working with sensitive or controlled data.
• Experience supporting or leading Configuration Control Boards (CCBs), configuration audits and engineering change processes.
• Experience with PDR/CDR and formal engineering development environments.
• French or German language skills.
Senior / Lead Configuration Manager:
For the Senior/Lead position, we are looking for significant Configuration Management experience.
The successful candidate should be able to operate autonomously, guide other Configuration Managers and improve Configuration Management governance, processes and data integrity.
The Senior/Lead profile should be comfortable resolving complex configuration and product-data issues, supporting CCBs and audits, and working across Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain and Project teams.

Additional Information
Working Environment:
The role is based in Pitstone.
Due to the recent PLM migration, the initial period will require a strong onsite presence for onboarding, knowledge transfer and collaboration with the existing team.
Initial working pattern: 3–4 days onsite per week.
Once established, there may be scope to reduce onsite attendance to approximately 1 day per week, depending on experience, project requirements and team needs.
Contract: Initial 6-month requirement, with expected extension.

Renishaw is a global, high precision engineering technologies group. Our Additive Manufacturing Group designs, develops and supports metal additive manufacturing systems that use laser powder bed fusion technology to build complex metal components layer by layer.
We are looking for a Service Technical Writer to join the team and help develop the next generation of service, maintenance and support documentation for Renishaw additive manufacturing products. This role will suit someone who can understand complex engineering systems, work closely with subject matter experts, and turn technical information into clear, accurate and actionable content for service engineers, support teams, distributors and internal stakeholders.
You will create and maintain documentation covering service procedures, maintenance tasks, fault finding, installation support, parts information, safety-critical instructions and product change updates. You will also contribute to AMG’s transition towards structured, reusable content using a Component Content Management System (CCMS), helping to improve consistency, governance and content reuse across the service documentation lifecycle.

•
Author, edit and maintain service documentation for AMG products, including maintenance procedures, diagnostic workflows, troubleshooting guidance, installation and retrofit support material, service bulletins, parts information and release-related documentation updates.
•
Work with service engineers, product development teams, systems engineers, software teams, safety specialists and product managers to gather, validate and structure technical information.
•
Translate complex technical information into clear, concise and accurate procedures for our global service teams that support safe and effective servicing of metal additive manufacturing systems.
•
Review and improve existing documentation to ensure technical accuracy, consistency, usability and alignment with Renishaw style, terminology and quality standards.
•
Support structured authoring practices by creating modular, reusable content suitable for use in a CCMS and for delivery across multiple channels.
•
Manage documentation tasks through agreed review, approval and release workflows, ensuring content is delivered in line with project and product change schedules.
•
Contribute to continuous improvement of documentation processes, templates, terminology, metadata and content governance.
Key requirements
•
Degree-level qualification or higher in engineering, science, technical communication, English, communications or an equivalent discipline.
•
Experience in technical authoring, technical communication, service documentation or a closely related engineering documentation role.
•
Ability to understand complex mechanical, electrical, software-controlled or industrial equipment systems and communicate them clearly to technical audiences.
•
Strong written English, with the ability to write precise, user-focused instructions, warnings, cautions, notes and procedural content.
•
Experience working with subject matter experts to gather information, resolve ambiguity and validate technical accuracy.
•
Excellent attention to detail, with a structured approach to managing versions, reviews, feedback and documentation changes.
•
Comfortable using Microsoft Word and CCMS platforms such as Heretto.
•
Familiarity with structured authoring formats such as DITA.
•
Good organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple documentation tasks and priorities across different product or service workstreams.
Desirable requirements
•
Knowledge of additive manufacturing, laser powder bed fusion, metal powder handling, motion systems, lasers, pneumatics, safety systems or machine control software.
•
Experience writing service documentation specifically for industrial capital equipment.
•
Experience creating or briefing technical illustrations, exploded views, diagrams, flowcharts or visual service procedures.
•
Familiarity with Jira, Azure DevOps, PLM, ERP, CRM, service management systems or engineering change processes would be advantageous.

Job Description:
The Role:
SiFive is looking for hardware engineers who are passionate about designing industry-leading CPU and interconnect IP to help drive the tidal wave of adoption of RISC-V as the architecture of choice for SOC designs across a broad variety of vertical applications. We’re creating massively customizable IP and improving time-to-market by designing hardware as highly-configurable generators. We're leveraging technology and ideas from the software industry to execute hardware design with the agility of software development.
As a Power-Management/Reset/Clock Micro-Architect and RTL Design Engineer at SiFive, you will be part of a team of engineers who are passionate about designing industry-leading CPU cores and subsystems based on the revolutionary open RISC-V and TileLink architectures. You will create power management, reset, and clocking solutions that provide the central nervous system for cutting-edge RISC-V CPU and SoC IP designs. You will work in a fast-paced dynamic environment to bring new hardware IP to market quickly, with high quality and exceptional performance - delivering hardware at the speed of software!

Work with the architecture team to understand and define power management requirements.
•
Architect, design and implement core clocking, reset and power management solutions.

Microarchitecture development and specification. Ensure that knowledge is shared via clear documentation and participation in a culture of collaborative design.
•
Perform initial sandbox verification, and work with the design verification team to create and execute thorough verification test plans.

Work with a physical implementation team to implement and optimise physical design to meet frequency, area, power goals.

Work with a software team to enable and optimise power management features.

3+ years of recent industry experience in CPU and SoC clocking, reset, and power-management logic designs.
•
Experience in high-performance, energy-efficient CPU and SoC designs.
•
Expertise in CPU and SoC clocking, reset design, and power management, including:

Reset control and design strategies: Clock distribution, dynamic clocking, clock gating, and clock boundary crossing strategies
•
Power state definition and management and Power Management Unit (PMU) design
•
Dynamic and static power reduction techniques, including retention and power-up/down sequencing
•
Dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) and Di/dt mitigation strategies
•
Understanding of DFT, MBIST, Debug and Error handling in CPU designs
•
Power-aware simulation
•
Proficiency with hardware (RTL) design in Verilog, SystemVerilog, or VDHL.

Attention to detail and a focus on high-quality design.

Ability to work well with others and a belief that engineering is a team sport.

Knowledge of at least one object-oriented and/or functional programming language.

Background of successful CPU or SoC development from architecture through tapeout.

BS/MS degree in EE, CE, CS or a related technical discipline, or equivalent experience.

Experience with AMBA Low Power Protocol Interface, including P-channel  and Q-channel protocols.

Experience with Scala/Chisel, Bluespec, or some other language/DSL for expressing configurable hardware via software

Knowledge of RISC-V architecture

Experience with Git/Github, Jira, Confluence

wiley.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/wiley_career.description_excerpt:
We believe in bold ideas, diverse perspectives, and the drive to transform knowledge into impact. Here, your curiosity fuels progress, your voice shapes innovation, and your ambition helps redefine what’s possible within science and learning. We are a culture that obsesses over impact, challenges, and drives what’s next to power infinite possibilities for our customers, colleagues and society at large.
About the Role:
About the role
We're building the systems that turn one of the world's largest scientific corpora into research intelligence. That means production NLP pipelines running over millions of journal articles, extracting entities, classifications, claim tuples, and summaries optimized for use by downstream agentic applications. We're looking for a senior data scientist to own domain-specific content modeling work end to end, from the eval set through the pipeline stage that ships it.
You'll join a small, senior team where data scientists own their models in production. You'll write the code, own the evaluations, ship the changes, and stay accountable for the outcomes. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to see their models through to real users in a rapidly evolving market.
What you'll do
•
Design and build NLP enrichment pipelines that extract entities, classifications, claims, and summaries from scientific full-text at scale.
•
Compare NLP approaches to extraction and enrichment against LLM-based approaches, and pick the right tool for each task. That means putting traditional NLP (NER, sequence labeling, classification), embedding-based retrieval, LLM prompting, and fine-tuned smaller models on the same table, and defending each choice with evaluation, cost, and operational tradeoffs. This is a core part of the job, not an occasional exercise.
•
Own evaluation. Build the golden sets in consultation with SMEs and vendors, choose the metrics, and make productive tradeoffs between speed, quality, and cost.
•
Write production-quality Python. Manage concurrency and cost for high-volume LLM workloads. Structure code that engineers can ship and other data scientists can extend.
•
Collaborate with a team of data engineers to orchestrate work in data pipeline and data build tools like Airflow and Dagster. Design idempotent, retryable, evaluable pipeline stages that stay reliable when a run fails at scale.
•
Contribute to agentic AI application work: tool-using systems that reason over the enriched corpus, where your NLP and evaluation background will shape how the agent grounds and defends its answers.
•
Work directly with editors, product managers, and engineers. Bring the modeling perspective into product decisions, and translate stakeholder pushback into concrete modeling work.
What you'll bring
•
Deep Python. You've written it in production, at scale, for years. You know when to reach for asyncio versus threads versus a queue, and you can explain the tradeoff clearly.
•
Strong NLP background across modern (LLMs, transformers, embeddings, retrieval) and classical (NER, classification, sequence labeling) approaches. You've built evaluations and learned from the results.
•
A habit of comparing approaches and choosing the right one for the task. You can defend "prompt a large LLM" and "train a small classifier on 2,000 labels" with equal seriousness, back the choice with an eval and a cost estimate, and know what to do when performance drifts.
•
A track record of shipping – not just prototypes and papers, but systems that deliver value to real users.
Nice to have
•
Experience working with scientific or scholarly text.
•
Familiarity with AWS (S3, Batch, Lambda, SageMaker) and Parquet or Iceberg data lake patterns.
•
Experience running LLMs under real cost and latency budgets in production.
•
Some exposure to agentic AI applications: tool use, multi-step reasoning, guardrails, and evaluation of trajectories rather than single-turn outputs.
Why us
We publish some of the world's most-read research, and we're now in a rare position: applying modern AI to a corpus of trusted scientific knowledge that spans two centuries. Researchers will use the systems you build here to move faster and get closer to the answers they came for. That's the work: from knowledge to impact.
We power infinite possibilities.
For more than 200 years, we've transformed knowledge into discoveries that shape the world. Today, our global team of innovators, creators, and experts is driving what's next in science, education, and publishing—creating impact that reaches everywhere.
We're not just observers of progress. We're the ones accelerating scientific breakthroughs, advancing learning, and sparking innovation that redefines entire fields and improves lives.
Here, your talent matters. Your ideas have room to grow. And your work creates breakthroughs that can change everything.

• Strong understanding of PCB design fundamentals for high-frequency and high-speed data rate applications
• Experience working within laboratory environments using advanced electronic test equipment
• Proven ability to generate, manage, and analyze large and complex engineering datasets

• Experience characterizing high-speed optical or electrical semiconductor products
• Strong understanding of high-frequency measurement techniques and signal integrity analysis methodologies
• Experience working with automated test equipment development and hardware integration

• Experience identifying process improvement opportunities and driving automation efficiency initiatives
• Interest in applying AI-based tools to improve engineering workflows and productivity

• Work on cutting-edge high-speed semiconductor technologies that power next-generation global communications infrastructure
• Collaborate with highly skilled engineering teams across an international and multidisciplinary organization
• Take ownership of critical product characterization activities that directly influence product quality and successful product launch
• Join an engineering culture focused on innovation, technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous improvement

POLITICO is looking for an experienced editor of impeccable judgment to play a leading role on our growing global standards and ethics team to ensure the integrity of our journalism across all platforms.
This hands-on editor will work side-by-side with reporters and assigning editors discussing sourcing and reporting questions as they develop and helping all journalists resolve knotty ethical questions as they arise.
They will provide a final edit on some of our most sensitive content, whether that’s a story, blog post or newsletter item, and address questions internally and externally post-publication as needed.
This senior-level editor will also take a leading role in writing and updating newsroom policies and stylebook entries to offer clear direction to the staff and work alongside others to assist on training and development programs for our journalists.
This role comes with a mandate to uphold POLITICO’s editorial values and commitment to authoritative, nonpartisan and tough-mindedly fair journalism.
This position may be based in either Brussels or London, but this editor should be able to collaborate comfortably with teams across Europe, North America and Australia.

•
Serve as a hands-on editor offering pre-publication guidance on reporting
•
Provide a final edit on sensitive content
•
Address and resolve issues related to our journalism after it is published

Help research and write newsroom policies and stylebook entries

Assist in designing training programs for POLITICO journalists
•
Ensure quality controls are in place across the newsroom
What You’ll Need
•
Written and verbal fluency in English

Ability to calmly juggle multiple tasks in stressful situations

Desire to collaborate with journalists across the newsroom, helping broker solutions to challenging situations

Excellent judgment and reasoning skills

Experience editing complicated and sensitive stories preferred
Let’s keep in touch
You can view our list of open positions here. We hope to see your application soon!
About Us
POLITICO illuminates the forces shaping global power. Since 2007, we have delivered intelligence that anticipates tomorrow's headlines, not reports on yesterday's news. As politics has increasingly become the defining force of our era, our work has never been more vital.
Cabinet secretaries and Ministers start their mornings with our analysis. CEOs shape strategy around our reporting. Advocacy leaders rely on our insights to move policy. We deliver the straightforward facts and clear-eyed analysis they need to navigate the most complex political landscape of our lifetimes.
Our 1,100+ publishing professionals across the world's key democratic capitals—Washington, Brussels, London, Paris, Berlin, Sacramento, and New York—form the world's premier politics and policy newsroom. We tell the story of how power really works by explaining who wields it and how they plan to exercise it, connecting dots others miss and delivering scoops from sources others don't even know exist.
Innovation has always been a core tenet of our story. At launch, we bet that depth would trump scale, that talent would trump traffic, and that politics would become central to modern life. In 2011, we made another bet and launched POLITICO Pro to help decision-makers understand the business of government, transforming both how they shape government action and the business of journalism itself.
These bets have made POLITICO the most successful digital news startup of its generation and the indispensable resource for leaders who shape the future. Today, we are a rarity in media: a growing, profitable, and sustainable news organization.
POLITICO is a subsidiary of Axel Springer SE, a family-owned transatlantic media company headquartered in Berlin and New York. Axel Springer is dedicated to shaping the future of journalism in the free world, believing that a free and informed society is essential to democracy.
