Job Description:
Production Planner - CROWN Packaging Manufacturing UK Limited
We currently have a vacancy for a Production Planner. The position is based at our Botcherby Plant in Carlisle and is a full-time role working Monday to Friday, 37.5 hours per week.
The Botcherby Plant is a major supplier of aluminium beverage cans, producing approximately 1.4 billion cans and over 6 billion ring-pull ends annually. The site operates 24/7 and plays a key role within our global operations.
This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced and knowledgeable individual to join a multinational organisation.
Job Summary
The Production Planner plays a critical role in ensuring the efficient operation of manufacturing processes by developing and maintaining effective production plans that balance customer demand, production capacity, and material availability. The role is responsible for optimising production schedules to ensure products are manufactured and delivered on time while minimising waste and maximising operational efficiency.
Working closely with cross-functional teams across EMEA, the Production Planner ensures production activities align with business objectives and proactively manages any disruptions that could impact supply continuity.
Key Responsibilities
The Production Planner is responsible for creating and maintaining detailed production schedules that support business requirements and meet customer expectations. Working collaboratively with Sales, Production, Procurement, Exports, Supply Chain Planning, and other key stakeholders across the region, the role ensures that production plans are aligned with demand forecasts, inventory levels, and operational capabilities.
The role is responsible for developing and maintaining production plans and schedules that support customer demand and business objectives, whilst ensuring alignment of production activities with forecasted demand through close collaboration with Sales, Production, Procurement, Exports, and Supply Chain teams. The Production Planner monitors raw material and finished goods inventory levels, identifying potential shortages, excess stock, and supply risks, and utilises effective inventory, stock, and forecast management techniques to optimise working capital and maintain continuity of supply.
The position coordinates production adjustments and material procurement activities in response to changing business requirements and is responsible for identifying and resolving scheduling conflicts, capacity constraints, and production bottlenecks to support efficient manufacturing operations. The Production Planner manages production orders, material requirements, and inventory transactions within ERP/MRP systems, ensuring the accuracy and integrity of planning data at all times.
A key aspect of the role involves reviewing production performance, analysing key performance indicators (KPIs), and identifying opportunities for continuous improvement. Corrective actions are implemented where required to improve planning accuracy, service levels, inventory performance, and operational efficiency. The Production Planner also supports engineering change management activities, ensuring that product and process changes are effectively incorporated into production plans with minimal disruption, whilst supporting wider supply continuity initiatives across the EMEA region.
The role is responsible for preparing and delivering regular performance reports to management, highlighting achievements, risks, challenges, and proposed solutions. Compliance with month-end processes, inventory control procedures, company policies, quality standards, and health and safety requirements must be maintained at all times. In addition, the Production Planner is expected to continuously seek opportunities to improve planning processes, systems, reporting tools, and ways of working, while providing flexible support to other site functions during peak periods, holiday cover, business-critical activities, and periods of increased operational demand in order to meet business objectives.
Qualifications and Experience
The successful candidate will typically possess a qualification in Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related discipline, together with a minimum of three to five years' experience in production planning, scheduling, or supply chain roles within a manufacturing environment.
They will have strong knowledge of manufacturing processes, capacity planning, production scheduling, and inventory management principles, together with experience working with ERP/MRP systems such as SAP, Oracle, JD Edwards (JDE), or similar platforms. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills are essential, with the ability to interpret data, identify trends, and make informed decisions.
The role requires excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage effectively at all levels of the organisation. Candidates must possess strong organisational and time-management skills and be capable of managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, is also required.
The successful individual will be able to work independently whilst collaborating effectively within cross-functional teams and will be expected to support other site functions during peak periods, holiday cover, business-critical activities, and periods of increased operational demand, providing flexible cross-functional support as required to meet business objectives.
Key Competencies
The successful Production Planner will demonstrate strong capability in production planning and scheduling, demand and forecast management, inventory optimisation, capacity planning, and supply chain coordination. They will possess a high level of competence in ERP/MRP systems management, data analysis and reporting, continuous improvement methodologies, problem solving, and decision making.
Success in the role will also require excellent stakeholder management, communication, and collaboration skills, together with the ability to build effective working relationships across functions and regions to support business objectives and operational performance.

performance related pay scheme (over and above basic salary).
•
an attractive contributory pension scheme.

private medical scheme, health cash plan and subsidised dental care.
•
life assurance scheme.
•
on site canteen.
•
cycle to work scheme.

leave during Christmas/New Year period.

25 days annual leave plus bank holidays

Alternatively, Grant Thornton
At Grant Thornton we do things differently, looking to the future, driving ambitious growth and pioneering positive change in our industry. Providing audit, tax and advisory services, we empower clients through strategic insight, curiosity and genuine partnership. And we empower our people with real opportunity, an inclusive culture and work life balance. A true alternative.
With over 5,000 people in the UK, and a presence in 150 global markets, we’re on an ambitious journey, from great to exceptional, with investor backing from our partner Cinven. We need the best people to help us achieve our potential. And with that comes the opportunity to help redefine what our industry looks like, and what you want from your career.
New ground won’t break itself.
Our Value Creation Advisory (VCA) team advises clients on how to increase the value from transactions, focused on business operations and working both pre-deal and post-deal. Integration is at the heart of what we do. We help clients plan and deliver merger integration that delivers sustainable value, from synergy assessment and operating model design, through to execution and benefits realisation. We pride ourselves on being highly practical, pragmatic and totally focused on what will make a difference for our clients. Every deal is different, and our approach and agility reflects that.
Our clients include public companies, privately held businesses and private equity investors. Alongside integration, we support clients undertaking carve-out transactions (both sellers and acquirers) and other initiatives that enhance EBITDA, including operating model changes that deliver cost efficiencies and support revenue growth. The goal is always to maximise transaction value at the point of investment, during ownership or on exit.
We work very closely with other Grant Thornton teams in the UK and internationally. These include specialists in technology, financial due diligence, corporate finance, tax, sale and purchase agreement advisory, financial modelling, financial reporting, restructuring and many more. Something which really sets us apart is how we combine the expertise at our disposal to form single client teams based on what our clients need, both in the UK and internationally.
A look into the role
As an Associate Director within the Value Creation Advisory team, you will:
• Lead smaller projects and play a key role on larger projects: integration, carve-out or other value creation engagements .
• Lead day-to-day client work for a range of project sizes, including devising and leading client meetings, undertaking analysis, preparing high-quality client deliverables and managing commercials and risk. You’ll work alone on some of our smaller projects and lead small teams on larger ones.
• Interpret and analyse a large volume of complex information, and identify and articulate the issues which are most important in the context of our work.
• Contribute to a positive team working environment, working effectively and enthusiastically with other Grant Thornton people, our clients and other parties. You’ll show leadership and always be prepared to get involved.
• Prepare sales proposals and pitches and support wider sales efforts, particularly working with Directors and Partners. You’ll have a track record of proactively building internal and external networks to generate opportunities through the qualification of leads, and will continue to do this at Grant Thornton.
• Support the wider team, particularly more junior colleagues, to learn and develop. You may also be a people manager for more junior colleagues.
• Assist the Directors and Partners with the day-to-day running of the VCA practice, leading internal initiatives and providing an appropriate level of delegation and support to other team members.
Knowing you’re right for us
Joining us as an Associate Director, the minimum criteria you’ll need to have are:
• Significant experience of delivering or leading post-merger integration, including synergy assessment, target operating model design and implementation including Integration Management Office (IMO), in an advisory context. In-house experience, in addition to advisory experience, would be beneficial, but is not essential.
• Experience in at least one other area of our work: carve-outs (including in a due diligence capacity) or wider value creation, such as defining and implementing revenue growth and cost reduction initiatives.
• Experience of leading small teams in complex, fast-paced environments.
• Extensive experience of preparing and reviewing high-quality written reports, Excel analysis and presentations. You will have very high attention to detail.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to tailor and adapt your style for different stakeholders and audiences.
• Project management and/or change management and/or transformation skills.
• Strong analytical skills.
• Excellent Microsoft Office skills, particularly PowerPoint and Excel.
• Flexibility to travel in the UK and internationally based on client requirements.
• Experience in the use of AI tools in the delivery of your work, while maintaining your judgement and the benefit of your extensive experience.

• Foreign language skills.
• An accountancy or other finance qualification.
Knowing we’re right for you
Embracing uniqueness, the culture at Grant Thornton thrives on the contributions of all our people. We never settle for what is easy; we look beyond to deliver the right thing, for everyone. Building an inclusive culture, where we value difference and respect our colleagues, helps our people to perform at the best of their ability and realise their potential.

Whilst on the EE Summer Placement Scheme you will work with a wide range of our hardworking and experienced electronic engineers in a friendly and encouraging environment. You will experience working independently, working in focused electronics teams, and working in dynamic multi-disciplinary teams, where you may be exposed to mechanical, software and servomechanism design, and you will have to work closely and directly integrate with them.
Each of these environments will provide invaluable knowledge of the company and our engineering processes.

Current undergrad working towards a degree in an Electrical, Electronic, Avionics, Electro-mechanical, Physics or related Engineering discipline.

You will contribute to independent credit opinions that the commercial mortgage securitization market depends on. Team Contribution & Capability Building

accenture.wd103.myworkdayjobs.com/accent.description_excerpt:
Digital Finance Transformation Manager
Career level: Manager (CL7)  |  Location: London / Manchester / Edinburgh  |  Practice: Finance Reinvention Partner (Platform Transformation)
Why this role
This is where a finance-transformation manager takes ownership of the design in front of the client. You'll lead the finance design on major transformation programmes: running the discovery, settling the process and enterprise-structure decisions everything downstream depends on, and holding the line on them with finance leadership. Much of that work sits where systems meet: where the finance core hands off to consolidation, planning and reporting, and where the enterprise structure has to hold across all of them. You advise on the right finance technology and target operating model for the problem, whatever the client runs, and you grow from here into a design authority clients ask for by name.
Accenture is a leading solutions and services company. Our strategy is to be the reinvention partner of choice for our clients and lead in the safe, widespread adoption of AI. Finance is one of seven Reinvention Partners at the centre of that, bringing the CFO agenda to life for clients: stronger performance, sharper insight, and better control.
"Our clients want a partner that can help them reinvent—boldly, continuously and at speed… while continuously building the most client-focused, AI-enabled great place to work for our people—our Reinventors." — Julie Sweet, Chair and CEO
What you'll bring
Fit-to-standard and finance process design. You lead fit-to-standard and process design across the core finance processes (Record-to-Report, Order-to-Cash, Purchase-to-Pay and Acquire-to-Retire) and across general accounting, close and consolidation, external and management reporting, intercompany, finance master data and finance controls. You take a client's requirements, run a structured fit-gap, and turn the result into a process design the business will run. That design closes faster, reports with more confidence, and strengthens control. Where the client wants something the standard doesn't do, you're the person who works out whether the answer is to change the process or change the design, and can argue either case on its merits.
Enterprise structure and chart of accounts. You can design and defend the finance backbone: legal-entity and company-code structure, ledgers, the controlling and profit-centre model, cost-centre and hierarchy design, and the chart of accounts across it. These decisions are expensive to revisit once a programme is moving, so you'll bring a point of view: what the reporting and statutory requirements demand, where a dimension serves better than an account, and how the structure holds as the group changes shape.
Finance design authority and senior stakeholder management. You own the design end to end in front of the client: chairing the design conversations, bringing options and a recommendation, writing the decision papers and driving them to closure. You work directly with finance leadership, from controllers and FP&A leads to process owners and the CFO's team, taking a contested design point, explaining the trade-off in business terms and getting an answer. You set the design standard for the finance workstream and coach the consultants around you.
Technology selection, vendor assessment and the value case. You lead technology selection and vendor assessment: framing the criteria, comparing platforms against what the client needs, and building a defensible recommendation and roadmap. You own the value case and business case behind it: the benefits, the cost of the change, and how the return on a platform investment gets tracked once the programme starts, argued in the terms a CFO signs off against.
AI in finance processes, and in how we deliver. You'll bring a working fluency in what AI is doing to the finance function, enough to hold a credible conversation with finance leadership: where it changes a process, whether reconciliations, close tasks, intercompany matching or forecasting, where it does not yet, and what has to be true of the data and controls first. You design AI-enabled ways of working into the target process: what an agent runs, what a person approves, where the human check and the audit trail sit. The same judgement applies to how we work. We're increasingly an AI-first delivery team, and you decide where AI-augmented delivery earns its place and what the team reuses. If your AI experience is newer than the rest of your track record, tell us what you've done with it.
Platform literacy and integration judgement. You've delivered on enterprise finance platform programmes (SAP, Oracle or comparable finance platforms) and you understand how one runs: how a design gets built, what "standard" means in practice, and what a technology decision costs downstream. Finance rarely sits on one system, so you can work through how the finance core connects to what surrounds it: the master data that has to agree, the interfaces between them, and the reporting layer reading from both. Where a process crosses that boundary, you design it to hold on both sides.
Target operating model and design-thinking delivery. You shape the operating model around the design: how the finance function, its shared-services or GBS arrangements and its process ownership need to work once the platform lands. You facilitate design-thinking workshops, co-develop solutions with the client in the room, and secure design decisions in an agile, iterative way, not through documents alone.
Shaping the work. At this level you start to see the next piece of work before anyone asks for it. You'll spot where a client has an unaddressed problem, shape a proposition around it with the team, and contribute to how we position and solution it. Origination and deal shaping are part of the Manager trajectory here, not something reserved for the level above.
Who you are
You take ownership and follow through, and you're comfortable being the person the client turns to when a design decision is stuck. You work well with ambiguity in a complex finance organisation and can hold a clear view without needing to win the room. You lead a team well, build trusted relationships across a client's management, and manage expectations and timelines when more is asked of the design than it can carry. You're closely engaged with what AI is changing in finance: you've formed your own view, and can advise a client on it instead of repeating what a vendor told them.
Things that set strong candidates apart: a track record (typically 7+ years) designing finance transformation on enterprise platform programmes; experience across more than one ERP or finance platform; work at the seams, where finance integrates with the systems and processes around it; leading a technology selection and the business case behind it through to a decision; depth in enterprise structure and chart-of-accounts design; designing AI-enabled ways of…

What will you need to succeed?

Job Description
Senior Manager, KYC Risk & Assurance

Who are we?
IG is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses. The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next. Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
What's the role?
This is a senior leadership role within KYC and Client Onboarding, reporting to the Head of KYC. You will lead our new KYC Risk & Assurance function, the pillar that gives first line real depth of financial crime expertise, quality oversight and risk decisioning.
Grounded in strong financial crime and compliance knowledge but operational and strategic in outlook, you will lead a team of three: two Enhanced Due Diligence Specialists who handle the most complex institutional and high-risk cases, and a KYC Excellence Manager responsible for process excellence and governance. Through them you will own first-line quality assurance over onboarding, the leadership of EDD and escalation decisioning, and continuous improvement across the KYC lifecycle.
As IG grows its institutional business and continues to uplift its financial crime framework, this role exists to build genuine financial crime capability within first line: making confident, well-reasoned risk decisions at pace, providing credible assurance to senior management on the quality of onboarding, and operationalising the standards and methodologies set by second-line Compliance. You will work in close partnership with, but independently of, second-line Compliance and Financial Crime, keeping the roles of the two lines clear.
What will you do?
Quality oversight and assurance
• Design, own and run a risk-based quality assurance framework over onboarding and EDD, assessing the quality and accuracy of risk assessments and decisions rather than only the completeness of files.
• Provide credible, independent first-line assurance to the Head of KYC and senior management on how effectively onboarding controls are operating.
• Own AML-focused management information and quality reporting into governance committees, giving senior management a clear, evidenced view of financial crime risk and control effectiveness.
EDD leadership and risk decisioning
• Lead the two EDD Specialists in delivering holistic due diligence and approvals on Prime and other high-risk clients to a consistently high standard.
• Act as the empowered senior first-line decision-maker on complex, novel or borderline cases, making well-documented risk decisions at pace and escalating to second line only where genuinely warranted.
• Own clear escalation pathways and turnaround standards for complex onboarding queries, so that decisions are timely and the client experience is protected.
Framework operationalisation
• Translate the KYC Standards and CRA methodology set by second-line Compliance into effective first-line procedures, checklists, training and business-as-usual practice.
• Lead the rollout and embedding of the KYC refresh process, covering both periodic and event-driven reviews.
• Oversee the risk-based remediation of the existing high-risk client population, prioritising the highest-risk clients first.
Process excellence and governance
• Own KYC process excellence and governance across the onboarding lifecycle, supported by the KYC Excellence Manager, driving efficiency and consistency alongside quality.
• Maintain strong standards for document and control governance, record keeping, and the minuting of key forums and committees, so that a clear and auditable trail of decisions is kept.
• Identify and lead improvements to onboarding processes, systems and controls as the business grows and regulation evolves.
Leadership and stakeholder management
• Lead, develop and grow a high-performing team of three across the UK and Poland.
• Build strong, collaborative relationships with the institutional onboarding team, Prime sales, second-line Compliance and Financial Crime, and senior stakeholders across the business.
• Partner with second-line Compliance on the design of KYC Standards and CRA methodology, contributing first-line operational insight while keeping ownership of the standards with second line.
What will you need for this role?
To succeed in this role, we think you'll need:
Experience & Education
• 10 or more years of financial crime and AML experience in financial services, with deep expertise across KYC, CDD and EDD and strong knowledge of the UK MLRs and JMLSG Guidance.
• Proven leadership of financial crime operations, KYC, or quality and assurance teams, including developing people and building capability.
• Demonstrable experience designing and running quality assurance or assurance frameworks over KYC and onboarding.
• Experience operationalising KYC standards, CRA methodologies and refresh processes into day-to-day practice.
• A track record of building AML management information and engaging governance committees and senior stakeholders.
• Good working understanding of the FCA regulatory environment. Bachelor's degree in Law, Business, Finance, Economics or a related field, and a recognised AML qualification (for example the ICA Diploma or ACAMS) is desirable.
Personal Attributes
• Acts with integrity and consistently demonstrates high professional and ethical standards.
• Combines operational delivery with strategic thinking, and is pragmatic and commercial in how they enable growth while protecting the firm.
• Exercises senior judgement with credibility and gravitas, and provides confident, effective challenge.
• A strong people leader who builds, develops and motivates high-performing teams.
• Communicates clearly and influences effectively at senior levels.
• Comfortable operating across the first and second line boundary while keeping the roles distinct.
• Demonstrates resilience and a strong sense of delivery and accountability.
• Comfortable working from IG's London office a minimum of three days per week.

Facilitate or participate on process safety reviews, including FMEA, Process Hazards Analysis (PHA e.g. HAZOP), Layers of Protection Analysis (LOPA), and Facility Siting Analysis across the region. Provide technical support to the region with the facilitation of these risk assessments.
·         Identify and assist implementing risk reduction projects to prevent major accidents, explosions, fires, and spills in USCA manufacturing locations.
·         Identify process safety training needs and organize training with support (if needed) of PPG Experts/Engineers/Coordinators or external partners.

·         Support implementation and maintenance of MOC and PHA programs.
·         Identify latest issues (such as regulation changes) within the country and communicate them to affected parties.
·         Network with other region process safety managers to foster adoption of best practices.

fticonsulting.wd108.myworkdayjobs.com/ft.description_excerpt:
Who We Are
FTI Consulting is the leading global expert firm for organizations facing crisis and transformation. We work with many of the world’s top multinational corporations, law firms, banks and private equity firms on their most important issues to deliver impact that makes a difference. From resolving disputes, navigating crises, managing risk and optimizing performance, our teams respond rapidly to dynamic and complex situations.
At FTI Consulting, you’ll work side-by side with leaders who have shaped history, helping solve the biggest challenges making headlines today. From day one, you’ll be an integral part of a focused team where you can make a real impact. You’ll be surrounded by an open, collaborative culture that embraces diversity, recognition, professional development and, most importantly, you.
Are you ready to make your impact?
About The Role
You will serve as a senior lead on some of the most exciting TMT communications mandates in the London market – working with a diverse range of clients, from listed technology and telecoms companies to rapidly growing private firms backed by prominent investors. Our TMT team offers comprehensive strategic communications counsel: managing corporate reputation and positioning, developing campaigns and narrative strategies, managing crises and issues, and fostering thought leadership.
Our work is intentionally diverse and exciting. One week, you could be creating a campaign that changes how a client is viewed on a complex issue, connecting with policymakers, communities, and the public through compelling, data-driven stories and earned media. Next, you might be managing a hot-button issue just about to unfold or helping a board find their voice on a topic that truly matters to their sector. It’s a role that rewards those who can spot the idea others might overlook and deliver it exactly where it makes a difference.
This is a senior position with ownership of client relationships. Though it doesn't involve managing a dedicated team of your own, you'll help guide the account teams you work with, maintain trusted adviser relationships with clients, and actively contribute to growing the practice.
Our London TMT team is a proud leader in its field, currently advising over 40 clients across sectors; from space exploration and digital transformation to cutting-edge technological solutions and beyond, all with a diverse array of needs.
What You’ll Do
•
Client leadership. You'll confidently manage sophisticated communication programmes, becoming the go-to person clients trust when it truly counts. That includes shaping corporate reputation and narrative, handling sensitive or contentious issues with care, and providing trusted advice to help clients find their authentic voice and communicate sincerely, even in tough situations.
•
Campaign leadership. You'll lead corporate communications campaigns, finding the angles others might overlook. You'll ground your strategies in research, data, and insights, ensuring your messages reach the people who matter most, whether they are policymakers, journalists, community members or the wider public. Your work will be instrumental in helping organisations shape opinions and foster reputations that last.
•
Account health and commercial growth. You'll manage accounts well - spotting and resolving issues related to budget, scope, and deliverables early on, turning challenges into opportunities. You'll nurture current relationships and build new ones, offering creative ideas to both existing and potential clients. Business development is a part of the role, not just an extra task.
•
AI-enabled advice and delivery. You'll bring a point of view on how AI and digital tools sharpen our work, from research and drafting to analysis, and pitch AI-enabled ideas to clients that drive genuine insight, efficiency and value. You'll help build that capability in the teams around you, choosing the right tools and setting realistic expectations about how they're adopted.
•
Leading teams. You'll be a leader on the account teams you work across, setting the standard for the work, giving actionable feedback, sharing your experience to help colleagues and clients work through the hard problems, and building strong partnerships across the practice.
•
Building the firm. You'll lead and take part in pitches and proposals, spot opportunities to introduce FTI's wider services to clients, and represent the firm's values and standards, including a genuine commitment to the letter and the spirit of our code of conduct.
What You Will Need to Succeed
Basic Qualifications
•
Senior-level communications experience, typically 7+ years, gained in an organisation with a strong TMT focus or in a senior in-house role at a TMT business. What matters most is that you've independently led significant communications mandates.
•
A strong track record in corporate communications: reputation and positioning, campaigns and narrative strategy, and counsel on sensitive or contested issues that draw media, policy or public attention.
•
A creative instinct for narrative and campaigns: the ability to find a fresh angle, build it on solid research and data, and turn it into coverage and influence.
•
Some demonstrated success in business development: winning, growing and retaining client relationships.
•
The judgement to advise senior stakeholders, up to and including boards and executive teams, and the presence to hold the room and stay calm when the stakes are high.
•
Excellent writing and the ability to make a sharp, credible case, whether in a boardroom or a pitch.
•
A practical, curious view on how AI is changing communications work, and a willingness to put it to use.
•
A collaborative approach and proven experience of working in an integrated way with multi-disciplinary teams
Preferred Qualifications
•
Direct experience across several TMT sub-sectors, for example software, telecoms, fintech, media, consumer tech or deep tech.
•
Experience working across regulatory, media and public audiences on politically or socially sensitive issues.
•
Experience of transaction communications: IPOs, divestments, M&A, fundraises.
•
A feel for how the media and information landscape is shifting.
•
An established network across the TMT, investor and media community, or a clearly demonstrated ability to build one.
